starting_principles: Definition of velocity as position derivative v = dx/dt
First kinematic equation v(t) = u + at
assumptions: Initial position x(0) = 0 so displacement s = x(t)

ordered_steps.action_description: Express velocity as time rate of change of position
Substitute the first kinematic relation v(t) = u + at into the differential
Integrate both sides from t = 0 (x = 0) to time t (position x = s)

ordered_steps.equation_latex: s = \left[ u t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \right]_{0}^{t} = u t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2

applicability_conditions: Valid for constant acceleration and initial position at origin
source_references: Concepts of Physics Vol 1 by H.C. Verma (Chapter 3, p. 48)
